title: sprint-02: forecast error audit and 7/30-day outlook (torrance)
goal: Measure how far published forecasts drift from what happened, then forecast the next week (published forecast, corrected only where CV shows it helps) and next month (climatology + decaying anomaly), each with a measured p10-p90 range.
pattern: batch ELT: raw -> staging -> marts (DuckDB) + per-lead MOS
findings: Published day-ahead max-temp forecasts for torrance (2022-01-01 to 2026-11-13, 1756 days) missed by 1.243 C on average; 20% of days were off by 2 C or more and 8% by 3 C or more (worst 7.4 C).
Forecasts issued 7 days ahead missed by 1.748 C on average; 16% of days were off by 3 C or more.
Bias: published max temps run -0.62 C at lead 1 over the whole period (positive = forecast too warm); it drifts by year as the upstream model changes.

Test window (2025-11-14 onward), max temp: kept the published forecast at lead none (no correction beat it in CV); correction lowered error at lead 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7; no lead got worse. The p10-p90 range held the actual value on 72.9% to 78.4% of days (target 80%).

min temp: kept the published forecast at lead none (no correction beat it in CV); correction lowered error at lead 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7; no lead got worse. The p10-p90 range held the actual value on 72.9% to 79.7% of days (target 80%).
Beyond a week: max temp lead 30: model 2.91 C vs climatology 2.86 C vs persistence 4.09 C; min temp lead 30: model 2.1 C vs climatology 2.3 C vs persistence 2.45 C.

01_outlook_next_30_days.csv.title: Outlook from 2026-11-14: next 30 days
01_outlook_next_30_days.csv.note: Range = p10-p90, aiming for 8 in 10 days inside. Measured on the test window it held: tmax short 73-78%; tmax long 66-74%; tmin short 73-80%; tmin long 70-74%. Days 1-7 use the published forecast, corrected where CV showed it helps. Days 8-30 are climatology plus a decaying anomaly, because no archived forecasts past 7 days exist to check the published 8-16 day values (shown as published_* for reference).

02_published_error_by_lead.csv.note: error = forecast - actual. share_off_2c = fraction of days off by 2 C or more.

limits: Actuals are ERA5 reanalysis for the grid cell, not a weather station; the last few days of the archive are preliminary.
Published forecasts are Open-Meteo's best-match model (previous_dayN hourly values aggregated to daily max/min), not a specific app's forecast.
Leads 8-30 have no day-level skill in any public model; the 30-day line is a seasonal expectation with a measured range, not a weather forecast.
One test window of 12 months; MAE differences under about 0.1 C are within noise.
Training rows are cut on target date, not issue date: up to 6 days of actuals just before the test window were not yet known when a lead-7 forecast was issued (about 0.1% of rows).
Temperature only. Rain is fetched but not modelled this sprint.
